title: Tag model and benchmark tests so mvn test runs only unit tests by an explicit marker, not by class-name luck
description:
Discussed with the user 2026-09-26 after TOOL-13 turned two probes into test/benchmark/ContractionBenchmark. That benchmark does not run in `mvn test`, but only because its name ends in Benchmark: the root pom's surefire configuration has no includes, so surefire's default patterns (*Test, *Tests, *TestCase) select tests across the whole test/ source root, and the `unit/**` includes exist only in the ixdar-app `test` profile. A mesh-backed check named ...Test runs on every build wherever it sits, and many tickets have nothing to do with the quad layout.

The suite is small (last full run with reports on disk, 2026-09-19 in the craw-2 worktree: 87 classes, 19 s; slowest RingCandidatesTest 6.0 s, CarveOneToOneTest 2.5 s, QuadLayoutNodeChainTest 1.3 s, QuadPipelineSeamTest 1.3 s), so the goal is a clear, enforced boundary rather than speed. Subsystem tags (e.g. a quadlayout tag that CRAW tickets skip) were considered and rejected for now: about 6 s saved does not pay for keeping them right; revisit if the suite passes a minute or two.

The design: JUnit 5 @Tag("model") on every test that loads a real model file and runs a pipeline on it, @Tag("benchmark") on every class under test/benchmark, and the root surefire configuration excluding both groups by default. Opting in is one documented command. Surefire applies the group filter even to a class named with -Dtest=, so the exclusion must be a property the command line can clear (e.g. `<excludedGroups>${ixdar.test.excludedGroups}</excludedGroups>` defaulting to `model,benchmark`), and `mvn test -Dtest=ContractionBenchmark` must keep working as CLAUDE.md documents.

Ixdar CLAUDE.md (Unit tests) already says a `unit.mesh.*Test` never loads a mesh file and never runs the pipeline, and four tests break it, each running QuadLayoutEngine on test/resources/quadlayout/figure_7/sphere_base_in_tri.off: CarveOneToOneTest, QuadLayoutNodeChainTest, QuadPipelineSeamTest and EmbeddedTMeshPipelineTest. For each, either rewrite it on a hand-built fixture (the *LayoutFixture classes under geometry/mesh/quadlayout/embedding/fixtures are the pattern) so it stays a unit test, or tag it model and move it out of unit/. Tests that run QuadLayoutEngine stages on a fixture mesh (GridMapOptimizerParallelTest, PatchGridSeamTest, QuadMeshExtractionTest) are fine as they are. Loader tests whose subject is reading a file (LoadMeshNodeTest, OffMeshParserTest, GltfMeshParserTest, GltfMaterialSlotTest) stay unit tests, but LoadMeshNodeTest should read a small dedicated file rather than a figure mesh.

Enforcement: a check fails the build when a test outside the model or benchmark groups reads a file under test/resources/quadlayout/ (a unit test in the suite that scans test sources, or an autofix checkstyle rule), so the rule in CLAUDE.md stops depending on review.

User ruling 2026-09-26: `ixd wt done` runs the model group too when the diff touches the quad layout, so quad-layout tickets still exercise the real-mesh checks before REVIEW while other tickets skip them. This part lives in ai-workspace (ixd/commands/wt/done.py, which already runs sync, the diagnostics check, the build and the launch entry): after the build, when `git diff HEAD --name-only` (plus untracked files) includes a path under ixdar-app/src/main/java/ixdar/geometry/mesh/quadlayout/ or a model-tagged test itself, run the documented model-group command as a `done` step, refusing REVIEW on a failure like any other step, and print which trigger path made it run. Otherwise print that the model group was skipped and why. The trigger paths are one constant in ai-workspace so a later subsystem can be added in one place. Keep ai-workspace CLAUDE.md, Ixdar CLAUDE.md ("Worktrees and git") and the `wt new` brief in step with the new step.
definition-of-done:
1. Root surefire excludes the model and benchmark groups by default through a property the command line can override; plain `mvn test` runs exactly the untagged tests.
2. Every class under ixdar-app/test/benchmark carries @Tag("benchmark"), and `mvn test -Dtest=ContractionBenchmark` still runs it (verified).
3. One documented command runs the model group and one the benchmark group (e.g. `mvn test -Dixdar.test.excludedGroups= -Dgroups=model`), both verified.
4. CarveOneToOneTest, QuadLayoutNodeChainTest, QuadPipelineSeamTest and EmbeddedTMeshPipelineTest are each rewritten on a fixture or tagged model and moved out of unit/; the ticket records which and why.
5. LoadMeshNodeTest reads a small dedicated resource instead of a figure mesh.
6. A check fails when an untagged test reads a file under test/resources/quadlayout/, shown failing on a deliberate violation and passing after.
7. Ixdar CLAUDE.md, sections Building and testing and Unit tests, name the tags, the default exclusion and the opt-in commands, and the existing mesh-backed-checks sentence is updated to match.
8. `mvn test` is green, with its summary line and time recorded before and after.

9. `ixd wt done` runs the model group after the build when the diff (tracked or untracked) touches ixdar-app/src/main/java/ixdar/geometry/mesh/quadlayout/ or a model-tagged test, names the triggering path, and refuses REVIEW when the group fails; on any other diff it prints that the model group was skipped. Verified on a quad-layout diff (runs), a non-quad diff (skips) and a deliberately failing model test (refuses). ai-workspace CLAUDE.md, Ixdar CLAUDE.md and the `wt new` brief describe the step.
testing-plan:
1. Record `mvn test`'s summary line and wall time on master.
2. Apply the tags and the exclusion; rerun and compare the test count against the classes that should have left the default run.
3. Run the model group and the benchmark group with the documented commands, and `mvn test -Dtest=ContractionBenchmark`.
4. Add an untagged test reading a figure mesh and confirm the check fails; remove it.
